editorNote: The first full week of October 1982 finds the cartridge wall thick with arcade translations and sports labels while Apple II owners still talk about Softalk best-sellers, spreadsheets, adventures, and action games in the same breath.
morningLine: Maze chases, baseball cartridges, Apple II shelf leaders, E.T. at the theater, and John Cougar on every Top 40 radio.

lead.headline: Coleco Sends Mouse Trap Into the Atari Maze
lead.summary: Coleco's Atari VCS version of Mouse Trap is listed for October 1982, bringing Exidy's arcade maze to a home-console aisle already crowded with Pac-Man followers, arcade licenses, and third-party publishers. Its arrival captures the week's retail mood: recognizable coin-op ideas were being repackaged quickly for living-room cartridge buyers before the holiday rush.
lead.confidence: October 1982 Atari 2600 release listing; used as exact-month shelf context for this weekly issue

market.headline: Third-Party Cartridges Crowd the VCS Rack

bbsNote.headline: Modem Owners Trade Tips After Store Hours
bbsNote.summary: Local bulletin-board culture remained small, phone-line based, and intensely practical: game hints, swap notes, and microcomputer troubleshooting traveled well before national online services reached ordinary homes.
